**Jämtland County** ([Swedish](/wiki/Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Jämtlands län*, [Southern Sami](/wiki/Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Jiemthen leene*) is a [county](/wiki/Counties_of_Sweden "Counties of Sweden") or *[län](/wiki/L%C3%A4n "Län")* in [Sweden](/wiki/Sweden "Sweden"). It consists of the provinces of [Jämtland](/wiki/J%C3%A4mtland "Jämtland") and [Härjedalen](/wiki/H%C3%A4rjedalen "Härjedalen"), along with minor parts of [Hälsingland](/wiki/H%C3%A4lsingland "Hälsingland") and [Ångermanland](/wiki/%C3%85ngermanland "Ångermanland"), plus two small strips of [Lapland](/wiki/Lapland,_Sweden "Lapland, Sweden") and [Dalarna](/wiki/Dalarna "Dalarna"). It borders the counties of [Dalarna](/wiki/Dalarna_County "Dalarna County"), [Gävleborg](/wiki/G%C3%A4vleborg_County "Gävleborg County"), [Västernorrland](/wiki/V%C3%A4sternorrland_County "Västernorrland County"), and [Västerbotten](/wiki/V%C3%A4sterbotten_County "Västerbotten County"), as well as the Norwegian county of [Trøndelag](/wiki/Tr%C3%B8ndelag "Trøndelag"). It measures 49,443 km2 (19,090 sq mi) and constitutes 12% of Sweden's total area, making it the country's third largest county. The capital is [Östersund](/wiki/%C3%96stersund "Östersund"). The [county governor](/wiki/List_of_governors_of_J%C3%A4mtland_County "List of governors of Jämtland County") and leader of the [administrative board](/wiki/County_Administrative_Boards_of_Sweden "County Administrative Boards of Sweden"), as appointed by the Swedish government, has been Marita Ljung since 2021.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

The county was established in 1810, at the time it consisted only of the provinces of Jämtland and Härjedalen, which is why the [coat of arms](/wiki/Coat_of_arms "Coat of arms") is a shield parted per fess with their provincial arms. [King Carl XVI Gustaf](/wiki/Carl_XVI_Gustaf "Carl XVI Gustaf") is occasionally referred to as Duke of Jämtland after his title of king.

Province
--------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J%C3%A4mtland_County&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Province")]

For history, geography and culture, see [Jämtland](/wiki/J%C3%A4mtland "Jämtland") and [Härjedalen](/wiki/H%C3%A4rjedalen "Härjedalen").

Jämtland County consists of primarily the provinces of Jämtland and Härjedalen, though minor parts of [Hälsingland](/wiki/H%C3%A4lsingland "Hälsingland") and [Ångermanland](/wiki/%C3%85ngermanland "Ångermanland") are also included, along with small uninhabited areas in [Lapland](/wiki/Lapland,_Sweden "Lapland, Sweden") and [Dalarna](/wiki/Dalarna "Dalarna").[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Administration
--------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J%C3%A4mtland_County&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Administration")]

The main aim of the [County Administrative Board](/wiki/County_Administrative_Boards_of_Sweden "County Administrative Boards of Sweden") is to fulfill the goals set in national politics by the [Riksdag](/wiki/Riksdag "Riksdag") and the [Government](/wiki/Government_of_Sweden "Government of Sweden"), to coordinate the interests and promote the development of the county, to establish regional goals and safeguard the due process of law in the handling of each case. The County Administrative Board is a [Government Agency](/wiki/Government_Agencies_in_Sweden "Government Agencies in Sweden") headed by a Governor. See [List of Jämtland Governors](/wiki/List_of_J%C3%A4mtland_Governors "List of Jämtland Governors").[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Demography
----------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J%C3%A4mtland_County&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Demography")]

Jämtland County is sparsely populated and more than one-third of the population lives in the [countryside](/wiki/Countryside "Countryside"), making Jämtland County the second largest rural region in Sweden, after [Gotland County](/wiki/Gotland_County "Gotland County"). However, most of the population lives in the rather densely populated region surrounding lake [Storsjön](/wiki/Storsj%C3%B6n "Storsjön"), commonly called *Storsjöbygden*, "the Storsjö district/countryside".[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Politics
--------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J%C3%A4mtland_County&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Politics")]

The county is dominated by the [Swedish Social Democratic Party](/wiki/Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party "Swedish Social Democratic Party") and the [Centre Party](/wiki/Centre_Party_(Sweden) "Centre Party (Sweden)"), which is unique in Sweden, but corresponds to the situation in the bordering Norwegian county of Nord-Trøndelag. The county is rather contrastive in the political field. While a majority of the municipalities are governed by [liberal](/wiki/Liberalism "Liberalism")-[conservative](/wiki/Conservatism "Conservatism") ([Swedish](/wiki/Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *borgerlig*, lit. "[bourgeois](/wiki/Bourgeois "Bourgeois")") majorities or by coalitions overstepping the bloc border, the [county council](/wiki/County_Councils_of_Sweden "County Councils of Sweden") is controlled by a [red-green](/wiki/Red-Greens_(Sweden) "Red-Greens (Sweden)") majority and the Social Democrats receive two out of four [mandates](/wiki/Mandate_(politics) "Mandate (politics)") to the [Riksdag](/wiki/Riksdag "Riksdag").

--------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J%C3%A4mtland_County&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Heraldry")]

The arms for the County of Jämtland is a combination of the arms of [Heraldry of Jämtland](/w/index.php?title=Heraldry_of_J%C3%A4mtland&action=edit&redlink=1 "Heraldry of Jämtland (page does not exist)") and [Heraldry of Härjedalen](/w/index.php?title=Heraldry_of_H%C3%A4rjedalen&action=edit&redlink=1 "Heraldry of Härjedalen (page does not exist)"). When it is shown with a royal crown it represents the County Administrative Board. Blazon: "Parted per fess, the arms of Jämtland and the arms of Härjedalen."

**Östersund Municipality** ([Swedish](/wiki/Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Östersunds kommun*; [Southern Sami](/wiki/Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Staaren tjïelte*) is a [municipality](/wiki/Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](/wiki/J%C3%A4mtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](/wiki/Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](/wiki/Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Östersund](/wiki/%C3%96stersund "Östersund"), which is also the county seat of Jämtland County.

The present municipality was formed in 1971 by the amalgamation of the [City](/wiki/Stad_(Sweden) "Stad (Sweden)") of Östersund with five surrounding rural municipalities.

Politics and governance
-----------------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund_Municipality&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Politics and governance")]

Swedish municipalities are responsible for government-mandated duties, and elections for the [municipal council](/wiki/Municipal_council "Municipal council") (*[kommunfullmäktige](/wiki/Municipal_assembly_(Sweden) "Municipal assembly (Sweden)")*) are held every four years, parallel to the [general elections](/wiki/General_election "General election").

### Political history

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund_Municipality&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Political history")]

Östersund gained a city council (*stadsfullmäktige*) in 1863, known as *Östersunds stad*, and each member was elected through a [single-winner voting system](/wiki/Single-winner_voting_system "Single-winner voting system"). Sweden was [democratized](/wiki/Democratization "Democratization") in the end of the 1910s and a more [parliamentarian](/wiki/Parliament "Parliament") election system was introduced. Östersund continued to be governed by the *burghers*, unlike Sweden nationally. The dominating parties were [the conservatives](/wiki/Moderate_Party "Moderate Party"), [the freeminded](/wiki/Liberalism_and_centrism_in_Sweden "Liberalism and centrism in Sweden") and the [social democrats](/wiki/Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party "Swedish Social Democratic Party"). The latter did become the single largest party in 1938 but due to a strong centre-right majority it remained in opposition. The only other party present in Östersund was [the communists](/wiki/Left_Party_(Sweden) "Left Party (Sweden)"), though they had little support in the city, having entered the city council in 1922 and lost representation completely in 1930. The conservatives was by far the largest party and had a majority of its own with 18 seats in 1922. After the municipal elections of 1950 the situation had changed. The conservatives was the smallest party with 10 seats, the liberals (now represented by [the Liberal People's party](/wiki/Liberal_People%27s_Party_(Sweden) "Liberal People's Party (Sweden)")) had 11 and the social democrats 19. This was in contrast to the turnout on a national level, where the social democrats had been the dominant party for over a decade gaining e.g. 46 percent of the votes in the [general elections of 1948](/wiki/1948_Swedish_general_election "1948 Swedish general election"). In 1952 a social democrat was appointed chairman of Östersund's governing body, due to the lack of political blocs and the strive for mutual agreements.

A majority for the social democrats was achieved first in 1962. The political scene was shortly afterwards altered, in 1966, when the [agrian and rural](/wiki/Nordic_agrarian_parties "Nordic agrarian parties") [Centre Party](/wiki/Centre_Party_(Sweden) "Centre Party (Sweden)") (previously known as *Peasant's League*) got into the city council, after broadening its scope to include non-farmers, alongside the [Christian Democrats](/wiki/Christian_Democrats_(Sweden) "Christian Democrats (Sweden)") (though not present on the national political scene) and the communists returning after a 40-year period of absence. *The burghers* was thus back in power. Following the rise of [Swedish welfare](/wiki/Swedish_welfare "Swedish welfare") the small municipalities could not cope with their assigned duties. As a result, large municipality blocks were introduced and *Östersunds stad* was heavily enlarged and several districts kilometres away from the city were included in the new *Östersund Municipality*.

The first election for the new municipality was held in 1970 and it was a large success for the Centre Party, both locally in Östersund and nationally due to its opposition towards [centralisation](/wiki/Centralisation "Centralisation"). Having entered in 1966 with 4 seats it now possessed one fourth of the total number of seats (which was mainly due to support from the city, not the newly included rural areas). Block politics formation became prominent and the Centre Party became the leading party for the centre-right block, whilst the Social Democrats came to dominate the left block. The Social Democrats regained power in 1980 and has since governed Östersund Municipality until present day (excluding a brief period in the 1990s) supported by the communists (after 1991 known as the Left Party) and occasionally the [Green Party](/wiki/Green_Party_(Sweden) "Green Party (Sweden)"). The Green Party has been in the municipal council since 1982.

**Östersund** (pronounced [[œstɛˈʂɵnːd]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Swedish "Help:IPA/Swedish") [ⓘ](/wiki/File:Sv-%C3%96stersund.ogg "File:Sv-Östersund.ogg"); [Southern Sami](/wiki/Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Staare*) is an [urban area](/wiki/Urban_areas_in_Sweden "Urban areas in Sweden") ([city](/wiki/Stad_(Sweden) "Stad (Sweden)")) in [Jämtland](/wiki/J%C3%A4mtland "Jämtland") in northern Sweden. It is the seat of [Östersund Municipality](/wiki/%C3%96stersund_Municipality "Östersund Municipality") and the capital of [Jämtland County](/wiki/J%C3%A4mtland_County "Jämtland County"). Östersund is located at the shores of Sweden's fifth-largest lake, [Storsjön](/wiki/Storsj%C3%B6n "Storsjön"), opposite the island [Frösön](/wiki/Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n "Frösön"). It is the only city in Jämtland. The northern part of the urban area is located inside of the municipality of [Krokom](/wiki/Krokom_Municipality "Krokom Municipality").

Östersund is the region's cultural and economical centre and by tradition a city of trade and commerce. The city had one of the most extensive [garrisons](/wiki/Garrison "Garrison") in Sweden prior to its closure in the early-21st century. Östersund is home to [Mid Sweden University](/wiki/Mid_Sweden_University "Mid Sweden University")'s largest campus site with approximately 7,000 students. With a total population of 50,960 (2017) Östersund is the [22nd most populous city in Sweden](/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Sweden_by_population "List of cities in Sweden by population"), the [46th most populous city in Scandinavia](/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Scandinavia_by_population "List of cities in Scandinavia by population"), and by far the largest inland city in [Northern Sweden](/wiki/Norrland "Norrland").

The city was the only Swedish city founded and chartered in the 18th century. Östersund was founded in order to create a trade monopoly over Jämtland whose inhabitants' lucrative trade annoyed the Swedish Crown. The intention was to persuade the local farmers to deliver merchandise to middlemen in Östersund, but the population opposed this economic philosophy, and Östersund long remained small.[[5]](#cite_note-found-5) It took until the end of the 19th century for Östersund to truly become a city, after the arrival of the railroad and the [economic liberalization](/wiki/Economic_liberalization "Economic liberalization") of that time.

Östersund is situated in inland Scandinavia and connected to [Sundsvall](/wiki/Sundsvall "Sundsvall") in the east on the Swedish coast, and [Trondheim](/wiki/Trondheim "Trondheim") in the west at the shores of the [Norwegian Sea](/wiki/Norwegian_Sea "Norwegian Sea"). Östersund is located in the middle of [Scandinavia](/wiki/Scandinavia "Scandinavia"), in the middle of Sweden, in the middle of Jämtland County and in the middle of Östersund Municipality. As the most centrally located city in Sweden, the city credits itself as the *[centre of Sweden](/wiki/Geographical_center_of_Sweden "Geographical center of Sweden")*.[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7)

Östersund is marketed as *Vinterstaden* – Winter City.[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9) Winter City as a project is run by the municipality together with city enterprises. While winters are long, the [local climate](#Climate) is only moderately cold by elevated and northerly Swedish standards, but with chilly summers. Östersund has had a long history as a centre of outdoor activities with a modern [cross-country ski](/wiki/Cross-country_skiing_(sport) "Cross-country skiing (sport)") stadium and an actual [piste](/wiki/Piste "Piste") in the city itself. Östersund has also hosted several [World Championships](/wiki/World_Championships "World Championships") in various sports such as [biathlon](/wiki/Biathlon "Biathlon"), [speed skating](/wiki/Speed_skating "Speed skating") and [ski orienteering](/wiki/Orienteering#Ski_orienteering "Orienteering") along with Swedish National Championships in cross-country skiing and [snocross](/wiki/Snocross "Snocross"). The city has been the applicant city of Sweden for several [Winter Olympic Games](/wiki/Winter_Olympic_Games "Winter Olympic Games"), but has yet to host one. The precursor to the Winter Olympic Games, the *[Nordic Games](/wiki/Nordic_Games "Nordic Games")*, were however held at several occasions in the city, due to lack of snow in [Stockholm](/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm").[[10]](#cite_note-10)

Geography
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n_and_%C3%96stersund_WorldWind.jpg/250px-Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n_and_%C3%96stersund_WorldWind.jpg)](/wiki/File:Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n_and_%C3%96stersund_WorldWind.jpg)

Satellite image of Östersund and the island of [Frösön](/wiki/Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n "Frösön").

Östersund is the only city in the province and is located on the shore of [Storsjön](/wiki/Storsj%C3%B6n "Storsjön"), the fifth largest lake in Sweden. The area surrounding this lake is commonly referred to as [Storsjöbygden](/w/index.php?title=Storsj%C3%B6bygden&action=edit&redlink=1 "Storsjöbygden (page does not exist)") and has been described as the world's northernmost located genuine agricultural society in the inland with [continental climate](/wiki/Continental_climate "Continental climate").[[11]](#cite_note-11)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/%C3%96stersund_from_Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n.jpg/250px-%C3%96stersund_from_Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n.jpg)](/wiki/File:%C3%96stersund_from_Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n.jpg)

Östersund and Frösön in February 2005

The city sprawls along the eastern slopes of lake Storsjön with most of the city, and the city core itself, located on the mainland, facing the non mainland part of the city, the island of [Frösön](/wiki/Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n "Frösön"), which for a very long time was the actual centre of Jämtland. Today, a sizeable part of the city's population live on the slopes of the island that face the city centre. Östersund is a bimunicipal town because a minor part of it, with roughly 400 inhabitants, is actually situated in [Krokom Municipality](/wiki/Krokom_Municipality "Krokom Municipality").

The city spans across *Östersundet* and the city was named after this strait. Östersund can be directly translated from Swedish to English as "East [Sound](/wiki/Sound_(geography) "Sound (geography)")". The name of the strait derives from an older [Jamtish](/wiki/Jamtlandic "Jamtlandic") name now present in the form *Åstersånn*.

### Climate

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Climate")]

Östersund has a [subarctic climate](/wiki/Subarctic_climate "Subarctic climate") ([Köppen](/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"): Dfc) and is located in the far north of the north temperate climate zone. The cold [Arctic](/wiki/Arctic "Arctic") winds that occasionally find their way to the city are called *nordvästan* ('the north-westerner') or *kallvästan* ('the cold-westerner') locally.[[12]](#cite_note-12)

The winter climate is much warmer than most locations at similar latitudes. This is due to the [Gulf Stream](/wiki/Gulf_Stream "Gulf Stream") and the many passages in the mountain range, bringing warmer [Atlantic](/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") winds to the city during winters. This somewhat [maritime](/wiki/Maritime_climate "Maritime climate") character also makes the summers in the city rather cool, in comparison to other towns in inland Scandinavia, which all have a more continental climate with cold winters and warm summers.[[13]](#cite_note-clim-13) It contains a strong influence of the [humid continental climate](/wiki/Humid_continental_climate "Humid continental climate") (Dfb) courtesy of its mild September lows extending the mild mean temperatures.

Though Östersund is in fact affected by the Gulf Stream, it lacks the high frequency of rain or snow following the currents. This is due to the Scandinavian Mountain Range acting as a natural barrier, receiving most of the [precipitation](/wiki/Precipitation_(meteorology) "Precipitation (meteorology)"), giving Östersund and the surrounding area a rain deficit.[[13]](#cite_note-clim-13) Another issue that has to be taken into account is the higher elevation of Östersund compared to the weather stations in [Ångermanland](/wiki/%C3%85ngermanland "Ångermanland") farther east. For example, [Sollefteå](/wiki/Sollefte%C3%A5 "Sollefteå") at a similar latitude 130 kilometres (81 mi) to the east but near sea level in an inland valley, has three degrees warmer July days. There is often [temperature inversion](/wiki/Inversion_(meteorology) "Inversion (meteorology)") between Östersund and lower areas in winter.

Östersund has a high exposition of sunlight and was the sunniest city in Sweden in the summer of 2007 (1 July to 9 August) with 654 hours of sun.[[14]](#cite_note-14) However, in comparison to east coast locations, sunshine is relatively low.

Cityscape
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Cityscape")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Draak_%C3%96stersund_22jul2006.jpg/250px-Draak_%C3%96stersund_22jul2006.jpg)](/wiki/File:Draak_%C3%96stersund_22jul2006.jpg)

[Storsjöodjuret](/wiki/Storsj%C3%B6odjuret "Storsjöodjuret") (the Great lake monster) is a [cryptid](/wiki/Cryptid "Cryptid") said to inhabit lake [Storsjön](/wiki/Storsj%C3%B6n "Storsjön"). This figure has often been used as a symbol for Östersund, along with the moose (see above).

Östersund was laid out with roads spanning from north to south countered by several [alleys](/wiki/Alley "Alley") from east to west, which is why an alley in Östersund is synonymous with a road leading down towards Storsjön. From the inner city one may gaze upon Storsjön, Frösön and the Jamtish [fell](/wiki/Fell "Fell") region with snow-clad mountains. This was made possible due to the [topography](/wiki/Topography "Topography") and the [grid plan](/wiki/Grid_plan "Grid plan").

The regularity in Östersund's road system and the slanting alleys leading from higher altitudes down towards Storsjön have created the "windows to the west" characteristic and unique to Östersund as a city.[[17]](#cite_note-17) The alleys, often seen as rather steep, have created the illusion that the houses in the city core are climbing to higher grounds. These houses were conformed upon their construction to fit with the slopes.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/%C3%96stersund_badhusparken.jpg/250px-%C3%96stersund_badhusparken.jpg)](/wiki/File:%C3%96stersund_badhusparken.jpg)

Badhusparken

The first city plan of Östersund was made with several large segments in the core being reserved as [green areas](/wiki/Green "Green"). Östersund was thus planned as a green city and special lots, e.g. *kryddgårdstomter* 'spice garden lots' were created along with construction lots. These lots shifted with a construction lot alternating with a spice garden lot. The garden lots are no longer existent since they too have been constructed upon. Many of the fences that separated each lot from another with trees and verdure were left intact. The large green areas are still present, with parks such as Kyrkparken, Österängsparken and Badhusparken being the most prominent. Badhusparken was once the location of a large [bath house](/wiki/Public_bathing "Public bathing") (hence the name *Badhus*-) though it was torn down in 1881 when the railway was constructed. A new larger two-storey pompous bath house was later built on poles a few metres from the shore, enabling the population to bathe in the waters of Storsjön during summers. This house was also torn down when a new bath house with heated water was founded in 1938.[[18]](#cite_note-18)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/%C3%96stersund_winter_festival.jpg/250px-%C3%96stersund_winter_festival.jpg)](/wiki/File:%C3%96stersund_winter_festival.jpg)

The national romantic Sparbanken building illuminated during the Winter Festival.

When Östersund started to grow as a city in the late 19th century the houses consisted predominantly of wood, though stone had become popular in the central parts. These houses were heavily characterized by [Neo-Gothicism](/wiki/Gothic_Revival_architecture "Gothic Revival architecture") and [Neo-Renaissance](/wiki/Neo-Renaissance "Neo-Renaissance") architecture.[[19]](#cite_note-19) A very common feature of these houses were [towers](/wiki/Tower "Tower"), some even resembling those on old castles like the one on [Hotell Grand](/w/index.php?title=Hotell_Grand&action=edit&redlink=1 "Hotell Grand (page does not exist)") at the main square. In the early 20th century a new age had come and in the main road, Prästgatan, the new age came fiercely. The wooden houses were replaced by stone buildings, because a city's well-being was measured in how many stone buildings it had. At the same time [military barracks](/wiki/Military_barracks "Military barracks") were constructed in connection to the older settlement.[[20]](#cite_note-20) [Jugendstil](/wiki/Jugendstil "Jugendstil") became popular too as an addition to the [National Romantic style](/wiki/National_Romantic_style "National Romantic style") architecture.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/Storgatan_in_%C3%96stersund.jpg/250px-Storgatan_in_%C3%96stersund.jpg)](/wiki/File:Storgatan_in_%C3%96stersund.jpg)

Storgatan in Östersund with an alley, a window to the west, down towards the Storsjön lake.

In the 1930s, the [functionalistic style](/wiki/Functionalism_(architecture) "Functionalism (architecture)") made itself apparent in Östersund's outskirts, which were growing. In the 1940s, the city was made more car-friendly and the city was first and foremost planned for cars.[[21]](#cite_note-21) Later sanitation issues were brought up, which resulted in the construction of a [sewage treatment works](/wiki/Sewage_treatment_works "Sewage treatment works") and waste water was no longer flushed directly into Storsjön. Östersund was also affected by the [Million Programme](/wiki/Million_Programme "Million Programme"), though to a lesser extent than other cities. During the same period older buildings such as Hotell Grand (to make room for Storsjöteatern), Cellfängelset (a jail located at the beginning of Prästgatan), Flickskolan (the girl school next to the city hall, where the current county library is located) and Västra stationen (at Badhusparken) were torn down. The local media described it as "demolishing madness".[[22]](#cite_note-22) When the Good Templar house was threatened in order to widen Rådhusgatan the city's inhabitants had had enough and the building was saved.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Storgatan_%C3%96stersund.jpg/250px-Storgatan_%C3%96stersund.jpg)](/wiki/File:Storgatan_%C3%96stersund.jpg)

Storgatan with a "spice garden lot" to the left.

The buildings along Storgatan (literally: 'the large street') with entire segments intact since the 1880s are considered one of the best preserved city settlements in Sweden. The wooden façades are rich with details and the house are relatively low, short and slim. A great amount of work was put down on creating a balance between details and entirety. Parallel with Storgatan lies Prästgatan – 'the priest street', Östersund's main shopping street. The buildings between the two streets are often connected and the streets create small rooms mostly inaccessible for keen winds. These so-called rooms also stimulate the social life on the streets.[*[clarification needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Please_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")*]

Stortorget – the main [town square](/wiki/Town_square "Town square") in central Östersund is one of six "closed squares" built in Sweden, the others being the ones in [Uppsala](/wiki/Uppsala "Uppsala"), [Karlstad](/wiki/Karlstad "Karlstad"), [Vimmerby](/wiki/Vimmerby "Vimmerby"), [Piteå](/wiki/Pite%C3%A5 "Piteå") and [Haparanda](/wiki/Haparanda "Haparanda"). It was created through indentation in four different blocks to deliberately create an open air room with openings to every direction, a style deriving from how cities were planned during [the Renaissance](/wiki/The_Renaissance "The Renaissance"). However the town square lost its original shape when it was opened up and expanded towards the lake. Stortorget has long been the city's main market place and core; it is also here that the thousand-year-old market *[Gregorie market](/w/index.php?title=Gregorie_market&action=edit&redlink=1 "Gregorie market (page does not exist)")* is held each year in March. The city festival *[Storsjöyran](/wiki/Storsj%C3%B6yran "Storsjöyran")* has Stortorget as its main centre.

### Districts and housing estates

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Districts and housing estates")]

Before Östersund was established the population in the area was very scarce. In [Odensala](/w/index.php?title=Odensala&action=edit&redlink=1 "Odensala (page does not exist)") and [Torvalla](/wiki/Torvalla "Torvalla") older settlements existed; the name Odensala can be derived from the Viking age and the Halls of [Odin](/wiki/Odin "Odin") (though Torvalla means 'dry wealds' with no reference to [Thor](/wiki/Thor "Thor")). These two villages were later incorporated into Östersund and are today two major urban districts. Besides them the urban districts of [Staden](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staden,_%C3%96stersund "sv:Staden, Östersund"), [Norr](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norr,_%C3%96stersund "sv:Norr, Östersund"), [Söder](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%B6der,_%C3%96stersund "sv:Söder, Östersund"), [Odenslund](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odenslund "sv:Odenslund"), [Karlslund](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karlslund,_%C3%96stersund "sv:Karlslund, Östersund"), [Körfältet](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6rf%C3%A4ltet "sv:Körfältet"), [Odenskog](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odenskog "sv:Odenskog"), [Lugnvik](/wiki/Lugnvik "Lugnvik") are found on the mainland of Östersund. On the island Frösön are the six urban districts [Hornsberg](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hornsberg,_%C3%96stersund "sv:Hornsberg, Östersund"), [Östberget](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%96stberget "sv:Östberget"), [Frösödal](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6dal "sv:Frösödal"), [Mjälle](/w/index.php?title=Mj%C3%A4lle&action=edit&redlink=1 "Mjälle (page does not exist)"), [Valla](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valla,_%C3%96stersund "sv:Valla, Östersund") and [Härke](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A4rke "sv:Härke").

The central parts of Östersund are a part of the urban district *[Staden](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staden,_%C3%96stersund "sv:Staden, Östersund")* – 'the city', which has become synonymous with Östersund for many people living in the nearby villages and towns. As Östersund is the only city in the area and nearest city for many it is common to call it *Stan*, though the [dative form](/wiki/Dative_case "Dative case") *Staa* has increasingly grown unusual. The residents of Östersund are referred to as *östersundare*, though local people in rural areas call them *stassbon* 'towners', and *stassbo* 'towner', in [singular](/wiki/Grammatical_number "Grammatical number").

### Landmarks

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Landmarks")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/Ostersund_city_hall.jpg/250px-Ostersund_city_hall.jpg)](/wiki/File:Ostersund_city_hall.jpg)

Östersund City Hall

The most well-known landmark of Östersund is the national romantic [Östersund City Hall](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund_City_Hall&action=edit&redlink=1 "Östersund City Hall (page does not exist)") [[sv](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%96stersunds_r%C3%A5dhus "sv:Östersunds rådhus")] (*Östersunds rådhus*). It is 51 meters tall, contains 136 rooms and opened in 1912. It is the greatest constructional symbol of the National Romantic architecture in Östersund.[[23]](#cite_note-23) The city hall looks almost like a fortress and has a particular connection to the local art of Jämtland. The [bell tower](/wiki/Bell_tower "Bell tower") is of typical Jamtish design, shaped like an [onion](/wiki/Onion_dome "Onion dome"). Local sculptor [Olof Ahlberg](/wiki/Olof_Ahlberg "Olof Ahlberg") (1876–1956) made most of the sculptural details and the ornaments are made from Jamtish [limestone](/wiki/Limestone "Limestone").[[24]](#cite_note-24)

Östersund City Hall was designed by [Frans Bertil Wallberg](/w/index.php?title=Frans_Bertil_Wallberg&action=edit&redlink=1 "Frans Bertil Wallberg (page does not exist)") [[sv](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frans_Bertil_Wallberg "sv:Frans Bertil Wallberg")] (1862–1935) and was seen by contemporary colleagues as the best of modern Swedish architecture.[[25]](#cite_note-25) The main part of the building is accentuated by a grand tower and a monumental stairway. It is accompanied by only one wing, the north wing, as the second, south wing, was torn down in the 1970s.[[26]](#cite_note-26)[*[failed verification](/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")*]

A recently built landmark is *Arctura*, named after Jämtland's provincial star [Arcturus](/wiki/Arcturus "Arcturus"), a large hot water accumulator tank. Due to its appearance it is referred to as *Termosen* ('the [Thermos](/wiki/Vacuum_flask "Vacuum flask")'). At night the 65-meter building is illuminated with various lights to give the appearance of sunrise and the [Aurora Borealis](/wiki/Aurora_(astronomy) "Aurora (astronomy)"), for example.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: History")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6stenen.jpg/250px-Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6stenen.jpg)](/wiki/File:Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6stenen.jpg)

The Frösö Runestone is situated on Frösön in Östersund.



Main article: [History of Östersund](/wiki/History_of_%C3%96stersund "History of Östersund")

Lake Storsjön's shores have long been inhabited. The area where Östersund is situated was for a very long time Frösön's link to the east mainland. Frösön, the island of the [Norse god](/wiki/Norse_god "Norse god") [Freyr](/wiki/Freyr "Freyr"), was originally the centre of the region and it was here the only inland Scandinavian [hill fort](/wiki/Hill_fort "Hill fort"), [Mjälleborgen](/w/index.php?title=Mj%C3%A4lleborgen&action=edit&redlink=1 "Mjälleborgen (page does not exist)"), was built around 300 AD. The ancient [Scandinavian thing](/wiki/Thing_(assembly) "Thing (assembly)") [Jamtamót](/wiki/Jamtam%C3%B3t "Jamtamót") was held on this island, the christening of Jämtland begun here and it was here the world's northernmost raised runestone, [Frösö Runestone](/wiki/Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6_Runestone "Frösö Runestone"), was raised.

Plans regarding the foundation of a [Swedish city](/wiki/Stad_(Sweden) "Stad (Sweden)") or *[köping](/wiki/K%C3%B6ping "Köping")* (market town, 'Chipping') in Jämtland existed among governmental officials already after the previously Norwegian province was ceded from [Denmark-Norway](/wiki/Denmark-Norway "Denmark-Norway") in 1645. [Queen Christina](/wiki/Christina_of_Sweden "Christina of Sweden") demanded the establishment of a [sconce](/wiki/Sconce_(fortification) "Sconce (fortification)") on [Andersön](/w/index.php?title=Anders%C3%B6n&action=edit&redlink=1 "Andersön (page does not exist)") shortly after the province became Swedish; this sconce would together with [Frösö sconce](/w/index.php?title=Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6_sconce&action=edit&redlink=1 "Frösö sconce (page does not exist)") secure Swedish control of Jämtland.[[27]](#cite_note-27) Christina's intention was to locate the "Jamts' city" within this [fortification](/wiki/Fortification "Fortification"). In order to construct the sconce the local inhabitants were coerced into [forced labour](/wiki/Forced_labour "Forced labour") 1651 but after protests and lack of [capital](/wiki/Capital_(economics) "Capital (economics)") the project was ended in 1654.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Old_%C3%96stersund.png/250px-Old_%C3%96stersund.png)](/wiki/File:Old_%C3%96stersund.png)

Östersund in the mid-19th century, the church in the picture was the first church in Östersund. When the houses were smaller it dominated the cityscape.

In 1758, the plans were brought back up through an initiative from the chief financial director [Pehr Schissler](/w/index.php?title=Pehr_Schissler&action=edit&redlink=1 "Pehr Schissler (page does not exist)") and the proposition did however initiate a new debate whether or not a city was to be established in Jämtland, in order to counteract the trading and [faring traditions](/wiki/J%C3%A4mtland#Provincial_character "Jämtland") of Jämtland's farmers.[[5]](#cite_note-found-5) Several other attempts at concentration had previously been taken, and deemed unsatisfactory.[[28]](#cite_note-28) Östersund was founded and given its charter by Monarch [Gustav III of Sweden](/wiki/Gustav_III_of_Sweden "Gustav III of Sweden") on 23 October 1786, shortly after the outskirt of the Odensala farmers' lands were bought for the purpose. Several other places had been suggested, like [Huså](/w/index.php?title=Hus%C3%A5&action=edit&redlink=1 "Huså (page does not exist)"), the then-largest settlement in Jämtland, along with [Krokom](/wiki/Krokom "Krokom"), [Sunne](/w/index.php?title=Sunne_(J%C3%A4mtland)&action=edit&redlink=1 "Sunne (Jämtland) (page does not exist)") and Ede outside of [Brunflo](/wiki/Brunflo "Brunflo"). Frösön was also a candidate but the lot fell on Östersund, as it was deemed most favourable.[[5]](#cite_note-found-5) The only things actually located in the area at the time were the main road and the bridge to Frösön. Östersund was upon its foundation freed from taxes for a period of 20 years and completely liberated from trade regulations and [guild](/wiki/Guild "Guild") order.[[5]](#cite_note-found-5) In other remote locations of the [Nordic region](/wiki/Nordic_region "Nordic region"), similar cities were founded, like [Reykjavík](/wiki/Reykjav%C3%ADk "Reykjavík") in Iceland the very same year, [Tromsø](/wiki/Troms%C3%B8 "Tromsø") (1794) in [Northern Norway](/wiki/Northern_Norway "Northern Norway") and [Tampere](/wiki/Tampere "Tampere") (1775) and [Kuopio](/wiki/Kuopio "Kuopio") (1782) in the Finnish [inland](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/inland "wikt:inland"). Östersund is however the only city in present-day Sweden to have been founded in the 18th century.[[29]](#cite_note-29)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/%C3%96stersunds_centralstation_01.jpg/250px-%C3%96stersunds_centralstation_01.jpg)](/wiki/File:%C3%96stersunds_centralstation_01.jpg)

The main railway station was built in 1879

The city developed poorly and had to struggle in its infancy.[[30]](#cite_note-30) The state tried to persuade the Jamtish traders on Frösön to migrate to the new city but they had no intentions of leaving such a rich parish with the fertile soils Frösön consisted of in favour of the swamp and marshes across the strait. During its first 50 years the city's population only grew by an average of eight people per year.[[31]](#cite_note-Rum-31) The city became the county seat of the newly founded county consisting of the provinces Jämtland and [Härjedalen](/wiki/H%C3%A4rjedalen "Härjedalen") in 1810, and a county council was established.[[31]](#cite_note-Rum-31) Though, Östersund remained a de facto farming village with fewer than 400 inhabitants in 1820.[[32]](#cite_note-32) An upswing occurred in the 1850s, as trade was liberalized and the logging industry developed.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/%C3%96stersund%2C_gamla_teatern.jpg/250px-%C3%96stersund%2C_gamla_teatern.jpg)](/wiki/File:%C3%96stersund,_gamla_teatern.jpg)

"The Old Theatre", originally built as an [IOGT](/wiki/IOGT "IOGT") assembly house in 1884. Now a hotel and a restaurant.

It took until the construction of the railroad in 1879 before Östersund became a real city and actually gained the status as Jämtland's centre, at Frösön's expense. Thanks to the "farmer chieftain" [Nils Larson i Tullus](/w/index.php?title=Nils_Larson_i_Tullus&action=edit&redlink=1 "Nils Larson i Tullus (page does not exist)"), the railroad came to pass through the city itself instead of outside it, as planned. The railway from coast to coast across the then-union between [Sweden and Norway](/wiki/Sweden_and_Norway "Sweden and Norway") was finished in 1882, connecting Östersund more closely to [Trondheim](/wiki/Trondheim "Trondheim") and Sundsvall. Östersund then came to grow faster than any other Swedish city. After ten years it had passed 20 Swedish cities in population.[[33]](#cite_note-33) The city attracted immigrants, a slight majority from the Jamtish countryside, though still with a high number of settlers from southern Sweden.[[34]](#cite_note-34) While Östersund was in its most intense state of growth, [popular movements](/wiki/Social_movement "Social movement") emerged among the inhabitants. In Jämtland and Härjedalen the [Good Templar movement](/wiki/IOGT "IOGT") (a part of the [temperance movement](/wiki/Temperance_movement "Temperance movement")) came to dominate completely. In 1883, 700 of the city's total population of 3,000 were organized Good Templars. The greatest symbol of the movements grandeur was the Order House constructed in 1885 in the city, *Östersunds-Goodtemplars-Ordenshus*. When one of the most prominent leaders, [Joseph Malins](/wiki/Joseph_Malins "Joseph Malins"), visited the city he announced that it was the world's largest order house.[[35]](#cite_note-35)

Many of the leading people behind the popular movements in Östersund saw industrialization as a significant threat to the native districts and the old village and farming community. The work from the movements made the city and its centre-right governance extremely hostile to industry. Instead they wanted to portray Östersund as a centre of [outdoor activities](/wiki/Outdoor_activity "Outdoor activity"), culture, education and tourism. Industry was not allowed to threaten the good environment and [cultural history](/wiki/Cultural_history "Cultural history") traditions.

In 1917 when the [Great War](/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") was fought on the continent and with the [February Revolution](/wiki/February_Revolution "February Revolution") in Russia, the beginning of the [Russian Revolution](/wiki/Russian_Revolution_(1917) "Russian Revolution (1917)") also affected Östersund. Rationing led to lack of supplies and a revolution was feared. Some of the citizens, primarily soldiers, went on hunger strikes and at the first of May that year 4,000 demonstrators gathered in front of the city hall demanding lower prices on milk and wood. The year after, the [Spanish flu](/wiki/Spanish_flu "Spanish flu") spread the world. The [city doctor](/wiki/City_physician "City physician") in Östersund noted that "Östersund ought without objection to have been more haunted by the flu than any other Swedish city", which is why Östersund was referred to by locals as *spanska sjukans huvudstad*, 'capital of the Spanish flu'.[[36]](#cite_note-36)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Stora_kyrkan_%C3%96stersund_march_2012.jpg/250px-Stora_kyrkan_%C3%96stersund_march_2012.jpg)](/wiki/File:Stora_kyrkan_%C3%96stersund_march_2012.jpg)

The large brick church was built in 1940.

Despite the [Great Depression](/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression") and several crises resulting in a very high unemployment rate, Östersund continued to grow in the [interwar period](/wiki/Interwar_period "Interwar period"). In 1918 the Odenslund area was [incorporated](/wiki/Municipal_corporation "Municipal corporation"). The business sector remained largely unaffected and Östersund continued to be one of the least industrialized cities in Sweden. Instead Östersund continued to focus on wholesale trade and became a centre for it in northern and north-central Sweden. The city's central position was strengthened when the [Inlandsbanan](/wiki/Inlandsbanan "Inlandsbanan") railway was constructed through Jämtland from the north to the south. The first scheduled bus route was created in the 1920s between Östersund and the nearby town of [Brunflo](/wiki/Brunflo "Brunflo"). In the next decade well over 40 bus routes were functioning in Östersund. The dairy was located west of the bus square, Gustav III:s torg, at the current site of the shopping mall Kärnan. This square naturally become a central part of the city.

Östersund continued to grow after the [Second World War](/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"). Lugnvik was incorporated into the city in 1954 and Östersund was, like the rest of Jämtland, affected by the [Rehn-Meidner-model](/wiki/Rehn-Meidner-model "Rehn-Meidner-model"), though not in the same way. The Swedish [Keynesian](/wiki/Keynesian "Keynesian") policy was launched in order to improve the mobility of the labour force. Jämtland was struck hard by this when the people moved from the countryside to cities, from inland to coast and from the north to the south.[[37]](#cite_note-37) As an urban area Östersund was affected by the [Million Programme](/wiki/Million_Programme "Million Programme") and urban districts like [Körfältet](/w/index.php?title=K%C3%B6rf%C3%A4ltet&action=edit&redlink=1 "Körfältet (page does not exist)") were created.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Unofficial_Flag_of_Jamtland.svg/250px-Unofficial_Flag_of_Jamtland.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Unofficial_Flag_of_Jamtland.svg)

Östersund became the capital of the Republic of Jamtland. Its [flag](/wiki/Flag_of_the_Republic_of_Jamtland "Flag of the Republic of Jamtland") can be seen throughout the year at the main town square.

The negative view towards industry changed when the [Social Democrats](/wiki/Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party "Swedish Social Democratic Party") came to power for the first time in the city's history in 1952. Industries were enticed to Östersund through the national localization policy and industrial areas were created in Odenskog and Lugnvik. Development was not, as already mentioned, as good in the rest of Jämtland as it was in Östersund and as a counter to the governmental policy, the [Republic of Jamtland](/wiki/Republic_of_Jamtland "Republic of Jamtland") was established in 1963.[[38]](#cite_note-38) Östersund became the capital of the tongue-in-cheek republic and the home of the freedom festival [Storsjöyran](/wiki/Storsj%C3%B6yran "Storsjöyran").

Östersund continued to grow and in 1970 [Frösö köping](/w/index.php?title=Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6_k%C3%B6ping&action=edit&redlink=1 "Frösö köping (page does not exist)") was made part of Östersund. In 1971 a major reform occurred in Sweden creating large municipalities replacing all the older institutions; the new large municipality was named after the city. As in the rest of Sweden, the public sector greatly expanded at this time. In 1960 the public sector of Sweden constituted about 30 per cent of Sweden's total gross domestic product; by the mid-1980s the number had grown to 65 per cent. At the time jobs were growing in the county council, the government and in the new municipality. The main reasons for the large expansion were the expanded [transfer payment](/wiki/Transfer_payment "Transfer payment") to the households that occurred along with growing interest and public consumption.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Everything was financed by heavy tax increases. The entirety of the 1970s was a period of expansion. Besides the new industrial complex the [Frösö bridge](/w/index.php?title=Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6_bridge&action=edit&redlink=1 "Frösö bridge (page does not exist)") was constructed, a new police station, Z-kupolen (burned to the ground in 1989), Storsjöteatern, [Folkets hus](/wiki/Folkets_hus "Folkets hus"), neighborhood churches, malls, etc. The county administrative office and the hospital were expanded and large residential areas grew up in the aforementioned Körfältet and Lugnvik areas, as well as in Odensala.

As early as the 1940s, the city tried to have a [humanities](/wiki/Humanities "Humanities") [university college](/wiki/University_college "University college") located on Frösön. Opposition between cities in Norrland was great and it was Umeå that finally emerged victorious in 1962. Östersund did, however, get a university college for social workers ([socialhögskola](/w/index.php?title=Socialh%C3%B6gskola&action=edit&redlink=1 "Socialhögskola (page does not exist)") [[sv](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialh%C3%B6gskola "sv:Socialhögskola")]) in 1971. Since 2005 Östersund has been one of the main campus sites of the [Mid Sweden University](/wiki/Mid_Sweden_University "Mid Sweden University") (Mittuniversitetet). A number of governmental offices have also been built in the city in recent years.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Garrison town
-------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Garrison town")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/F4tva%29.JPG/250px-F4tva%29.JPG)](/wiki/File:F4tva).JPG)

[Hangar](/wiki/Hangar "Hangar") on Frösön

Östersund became a [garrison town](/wiki/Garrison "Garrison") when the [Norrland Artillery Regiment](/wiki/Norrland_Artillery_Regiment "Norrland Artillery Regiment") (A 4) was founded in the city in 1892, followed by the upgrading of the [Jämtland Ranger Corps](/wiki/J%C3%A4mtland_Ranger_Corps "Jämtland Ranger Corps") to the [Jämtland Ranger Regiment](/wiki/J%C3%A4mtland_Ranger_Corps "Jämtland Ranger Corps") (I 23). This was done with the growing fear of a Russian assault whereas Jämtland-Trøndelag and [Norrbotten](/wiki/Norrbotten "Norrbotten") became the most prioritized defense regions. The [dissolution of the union between Sweden and Norway](/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_union_between_Norway_and_Sweden_in_1905 "Dissolution of the union between Norway and Sweden in 1905") contributed by enhancing Östersund as a military city and strengthening its presence; the Jämtland Ranger Regiment was located in the city in 1910 and the [Jämtland Wing](/wiki/J%C3%A4mtland_Wing "Jämtland Wing") (F 4) came to Frösön in 1926.

Östersund's importance as a garrison town grew when the city was connected to the [Boden Fortress](/wiki/Boden_Fortress "Boden Fortress"), following the construction of the Inlandsbanan railway.

After the fall of the [Iron Curtain](/wiki/Iron_Curtain "Iron Curtain"), the destruction of the [Berlin Wall](/wiki/Berlin_Wall "Berlin Wall") in 1989 and the [Dissolution of the USSR](/wiki/History_of_the_Soviet_Union_(1985%E2%80%931991)#Dissolution_of_the_USSR "History of the Soviet Union (1985–1991)") in 1991 Sweden had lost its national threat and the demand for a strong defense organization was deemed unnecessary. The issue was debated throughout the 1990s and the final decision came in 2004 where all military presence in Östersund was ended. Upon delivering the message the [Swedish Minister for Defence](/wiki/Minister_for_Defence_(Sweden) "Minister for Defence (Sweden)") [Leni Björklund](/wiki/Leni_Bj%C3%B6rklund "Leni Björklund") was publicly [booed](/wiki/Booing "Booing") by the city's inhabitants.

The ending of Östersund's status as a garrison town has however created larger enthusiasm regarding the city's future[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] as the [private sector](/wiki/Private_sector "Private sector") has grown larger and more companies are being established, much of which is due to the financial compensation offered by the state. The older areas reserved for military activities have been opened up and two more urban districts were made available.

Politics and governance
-----------------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Politics and governance")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Stadsvapensflagga_framf%C3%B6r_%C3%96stersunds_r%C3%A5dhus.jpg/250px-Stadsvapensflagga_framf%C3%B6r_%C3%96stersunds_r%C3%A5dhus.jpg)](/wiki/File:Stadsvapensflagga_framf%C3%B6r_%C3%96stersunds_r%C3%A5dhus.jpg)

Östersund Municipality is governed from the city hall.



Main article: [Östersund Municipality](/wiki/%C3%96stersund_Municipality "Östersund Municipality")

Östersund is the capital of Jämtland County and thus, the county governor [Britt Bohlin Ohlsson](/w/index.php?title=Britt_Bohlin_Ohlsson&action=edit&redlink=1 "Britt Bohlin Ohlsson (page does not exist)") resides in the city. Bohlin Ohlsson is the head of [Jämtland County Administrative Board](/wiki/County_Administrative_Boards_of_Sweden "County Administrative Boards of Sweden") (*Länsstyrelsen i Jämtlands län*), an administrative entity appointed by the [Swedish Government](/wiki/Government_of_Sweden "Government of Sweden").

Östersund is also the seat of [Jämtland County Council](/w/index.php?title=J%C3%A4mtland_County_Council&action=edit&redlink=1 "Jämtland County Council (page does not exist)") (*Jämtlands läns landsting*). The County Council is the elected assembly of Jämtland County. The County Council's responsibilities lie primarily within the [public health care](/wiki/Publicly_funded_health_care "Publicly funded health care") system and transportation between the municipalities.

Östersund is the seat of [Östersund Municipality](/wiki/%C3%96stersund_Municipality "Östersund Municipality") (*Östersunds kommun*). The legislative body of the municipality is the 67-member municipal assembly (*[kommunfullmäktige](/wiki/Kommunfullm%C3%A4ktige "Kommunfullmäktige")*), elected by proportional representation for a four-year term. The assembly appoints the municipality's main governing body, the 15-member executive committee (*kommunstyrelsen*). The executive committee is headed by the Mayor (*kommunstyrelsens ordförande*). Östersund has historically been dominated by [the Conservatives](/wiki/Moderate_Party "Moderate Party"), [the freeminded](/wiki/Liberalism_and_centrism_in_Sweden "Liberalism and centrism in Sweden") (later on [Liberal People's Party](/wiki/Liberal_People%27s_Party_(Sweden) "Liberal People's Party (Sweden)")) and the [Social Democrats](/wiki/Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party "Swedish Social Democratic Party"). Though contrary to Sweden on a national level, Östersund's centre-right parties long remained in majority. The situation changed only in 1952 when the Social Democrats were included and they won an absolute majority in 1962. In 1966 the [agrarian and rural](/wiki/Nordic_Agrarian_parties "Nordic Agrarian parties") [Centre Party](/wiki/Centre_Party_(Sweden) "Centre Party (Sweden)") entered the scene, along with the minor [Christian Democrat](/wiki/Christian_Democrats_(Sweden) "Christian Democrats (Sweden)") and [Communist](/wiki/Left_Party_(Sweden) "Left Party (Sweden)") parties. A new centre-right municipal government was appointed and the Centre Party became the largest party in that coalition in 1970. However, since the 1980s the Social Democratic Party has been in power (excluding a term in the 1990s) supported by the communists (now Left Party) and occasionally the [Green Party](/wiki/Green_Party_(Sweden) "Green Party (Sweden)") (entered in 1982).
Jens Nilsson from the Social Democratic Party is the mayor of Östersund and has been so since 1997.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Transport
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Transport")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/%C3%85re_%C3%B6stersund_flygplats.jpg/250px-%C3%85re_%C3%B6stersund_flygplats.jpg)](/wiki/File:%C3%85re_%C3%B6stersund_flygplats.jpg)

In 2006 [Åre](/wiki/%C3%85re "Åre") was included in the airport's name, in order to emphasize its role as a gateway to Sweden's largest ski resort.[[39]](#cite_note-39)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6bron.jpg/250px-Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6bron.jpg)](/wiki/File:Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6bron.jpg)

Frösö Bridge

The airport is situated 11 km (7 mi) outside the city centre, on the island of Frösön. [Åre Östersund Airport](/wiki/%C3%85re_%C3%96stersund_Airport "Åre Östersund Airport") (previously named *Östersunds flygplats*) is an [international airport](/wiki/International_airport "International airport") and the ninth biggest in Sweden with roughly 390,000 passengers in 2005. The airport is one of few Swedish airports with incoming foreign charter traffic and the only one with considerable economic growth in that sector.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

The [European route E14](/wiki/European_route_E14 "European route E14") runs through Östersund from Trondheim to [Sundsvall](/wiki/Sundsvall "Sundsvall") and briefly merges with the [European route E45](/wiki/European_route_E45 "European route E45") (referred to as [Inlandsvägen](/wiki/Inlandsv%C3%A4gen "Inlandsvägen") locally) coming from the north. The two roads are later split in [Brunflo](/wiki/Brunflo "Brunflo") where E14 continues heading east and E45 turns south again.

Östersund has passenger rail services to and from, mainly, Sundsvall and Stockholm. [Norrtåg](/wiki/Norrt%C3%A5g "Norrtåg") operates [Mittbanan](/wiki/Mittbanan "Mittbanan") from [Storlien](/wiki/Storlien "Storlien") to Sundsvall. [Inlandsbanan](/wiki/Inlandsbanan "Inlandsbanan") runs in the same directions as European Route 45. Östersund is connected to Stockholm via long distance [SJ 3000](/wiki/SJ_3000 "SJ 3000") ([higher-speed trains](/wiki/Higher-speed_rail "Higher-speed rail")), [InterCity](/wiki/InterCity "InterCity") and night train. There are overnight services to and from [Gothenburg](/wiki/Gothenburg "Gothenburg") and, seasonally, [Malmö](/wiki/Malm%C3%B6 "Malmö"). Local company Stadsbussarna i Östersund (literally: 'the City Buses in Östersund') has nine routes in the city.

As Östersund is located on the shores of Storsjön, (English: 'the great lake'), it also has a [harbour](/wiki/Harbour "Harbour"). There is also a harbour on the Frösö side of the strait. Several bridges span across Storsjön connecting Östersund with communities nearby, [Frösöbron](/w/index.php?title=Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6bron&action=edit&redlink=1 "Frösöbron (page does not exist)") across Östersundet, [Vallsundsbron](/w/index.php?title=Vallsundsbron&action=edit&redlink=1 "Vallsundsbron (page does not exist)") from Frösön across Vallsundet to *Annersia* 'the other side' and [Rödöbron](/w/index.php?title=R%C3%B6d%C3%B6bron&action=edit&redlink=1 "Rödöbron (page does not exist)") from Frösön to Rödön in Krokom Municipality.

Trade and commerce
------------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Trade and commerce")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Ostersund.JPG/250px-Ostersund.JPG)](/wiki/File:Ostersund.JPG)

Prästgatan

Like the rest of Jämtland Östersund is heavily dominated by many [small businesses](/wiki/Small_business "Small business"). The city is the centre of trade and commerce in Jämtland County and has more than 300 shops. The [retail trade](/wiki/Retailing "Retailing")'s [turnover](/wiki/Revenue "Revenue") is 30 per cent higher than it ought to be, given the number of inhabitants the city has.[[40]](#cite_note-40) Trade in the central business district (*Staden* – 'the city') is mostly concentrated on the shopping and pedestrian street Prästgatan where large local shopping malls such as Kärnan and Mittpunkten along with department stores such as [Åhléns](/wiki/%C3%85hl%C3%A9ns "Åhléns") are located. There are large clothing companies such as [H&M](/wiki/H%26M "H&M") and [Lindex](/wiki/Lindex "Lindex") and smaller ones like [WESC](/wiki/WESC "WESC"), approximately 50 restaurants, shoe stores, sporting goods retailers like Stadium and [Intersport](/wiki/Intersport "Intersport"), several supermarkets (Östersund has rather few convenience stores), etc. Storgatan, the street that runs parallel with Prästgatan, is also lined with shops, restaurants and coffeehouses. Unlike Prästgatan this street is not a pedestrian street. Östersund is the city in Sweden with the most square metres of window display per capita.[[41]](#cite_note-41) The most prominent figure in Östersund's business life throughout the 20th century was the car salesman (who started out selling horses) [Sven O. Persson](/w/index.php?title=Sven_O._Persson&action=edit&redlink=1 "Sven O. Persson (page does not exist)"), founder of [Persson Invest](/w/index.php?title=Persson_Invest&action=edit&redlink=1 "Persson Invest (page does not exist)"), [Byggelit](/w/index.php?title=Byggelit&action=edit&redlink=1 "Byggelit (page does not exist)") and [Bilbolaget](/w/index.php?title=Bilbolaget&action=edit&redlink=1 "Bilbolaget (page does not exist)").[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] A significant real estate owner was [Maths O. Sundqvist](/wiki/Maths_O._Sundqvist "Maths O. Sundqvist") (1950–2012).

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/Storgatan_i_%C3%96stersund.jpg/250px-Storgatan_i_%C3%96stersund.jpg)](/wiki/File:Storgatan_i_%C3%96stersund.jpg)

Storgatan in late afternoon.

Östersund has had a long history as a [marketplace](/wiki/Marketplace "Marketplace") with the already mentioned ancient Gregorie market, tracing its lineage back to the 11th century, held in early March.[[42]](#cite_note-42) Despite being banned in 1914, it continued to be held for a couple of years. In 1950, the market was reborn shortly and was completely resurrected in 1986, when the city celebrated its 200th anniversary, and has been held yearly since then.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] In 1948, when the markets were non-existent, visions to restore Östersund's market traditions in a modern version were brought up. The result was the [trade fair](/wiki/Trade_fair "Trade fair") [Expo Norr](/w/index.php?title=Expo_Norr&action=edit&redlink=1 "Expo Norr (page does not exist)"), initiated in 1950 in order to strengthen Östersund as a leading centre of trade in the northern parts of Sweden. The trade fair is an annual event just like Gregorie market, though Expo Norr is held during the summer and not during the winter. Expo Norr is usually attended by 30,000 individuals every year.

Like many other county capitals in Sweden the [county council](/w/index.php?title=J%C3%A4mtland_County_Council&action=edit&redlink=1 "Jämtland County Council (page does not exist)") and the municipality are among the largest employers.

Besides trading and [public services](/wiki/Public_services "Public services") Östersund has some larger companies such as [Solectron](/wiki/Solectron "Solectron"), [Cybercom](/w/index.php?title=Cybercom_AB&action=edit&redlink=1 "Cybercom AB (page does not exist)"), [Volex](/w/index.php?title=Volex&action=edit&redlink=1 "Volex (page does not exist)"), [Husqvarna AB](/wiki/Husqvarna_AB "Husqvarna AB"), [Swedbank](/wiki/Swedbank "Swedbank")'s telephone bank and [Telia](/wiki/Telia_(company) "Telia (company)").[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Companies such as the dairy cooperation [Milko](/wiki/Milko_(Swedish_cooperative) "Milko (Swedish cooperative)") and [Inlandsbanan AB](/w/index.php?title=Inlandsbanan_AB&action=edit&redlink=1 "Inlandsbanan AB (page does not exist)") have located their [corporate headquarters](/wiki/Corporate_headquarters "Corporate headquarters") in the city.

A national survey done by the [Confederation of Swedish Enterprise](/wiki/Confederation_of_Swedish_Enterprise "Confederation of Swedish Enterprise") shows that out of every company in Östersund Municipality 52 per cent are "very positive towards [globalization](/wiki/Globalization "Globalization")", thus ranking Östersund at number eight in Sweden as the most globalization-friendly municipality (2008).[[43]](#cite_note-43)

Culture
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Culture")]

### Cultural venues

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Cultural venues")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Thom%C3%A9e.jpg/250px-Thom%C3%A9e.jpg)](/wiki/File:Thom%C3%A9e.jpg)

S/S *Thomée* moored in the harbour.

Östersund is the cultural centre of Jämtland County and home to the prize winning museum [Jamtli](/wiki/Jamtli "Jamtli"). The museum has both an indoor exhibition area and an outdoor area which contains a number of historical buildings from all over the county, depicting the old lives of peasants, the early city of Östersund and the Scandinavian inland herding. The museum exhibition hosts an interesting set of tapestries, the *[Överhogdal tapestries](/wiki/%C3%96verhogdal_tapestries "Överhogdal tapestries")*, showing a rich imagery of both Norse and Christian origin from the [Viking Age](/wiki/Viking_Age "Viking Age"). The mythical [Storsjöodjuret](/wiki/Storsj%C3%B6odjuret "Storsjöodjuret") (Great Lake Monster) has an exhibit of its own. Another remnant from the Viking Age is [Frösöstenen](/wiki/Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6stenen "Frösöstenen"), one of the world's most northerly rune stones located on Frösön, the island of [Freyr](/wiki/Freyr "Freyr").

The county library, Jämtlands läns bibliotek, is located in the city. It is the oldest county library in Sweden, being founded in 1816 by the will of professor [Carl Zetterström](/w/index.php?title=Carl_Zetterstr%C3%B6m&action=edit&redlink=1 "Carl Zetterström (page does not exist)"). As the library grew it was moved to a bigger facility. The older building is now situated beside the old church in Kyrkparken.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Moose_Zoo_%C3%96stersund.jpg/250px-Moose_Zoo_%C3%96stersund.jpg)](/wiki/File:Moose_Zoo_%C3%96stersund.jpg)

Moose Garden

Lake Storsjön has been trafficked for a long time and the [steamships](/wiki/Steamship "Steamship") [S/S Thomée](/w/index.php?title=S/S_Thom%C3%A9e&action=edit&redlink=1 "S/S Thomée (page does not exist)") and [S/S Östersund](/w/index.php?title=S/S_%C3%96stersund&action=edit&redlink=1 "S/S Östersund (page does not exist)") are still in operation every summer. Unlike most boats, they are seen as male and not female. S/S Thomée is the only one that sets sail from Östersund's harbour. S/S Östersund sails from Arvesund, located at Storsjön's western shore but makes visits to Jamtli's steamboat jetty.

[Frösö Zoo](/wiki/Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6_Zoo "Frösö Zoo") was one of Sweden's largest [zoological gardens](/wiki/Zoological_garden "Zoological garden") with [exotic animals](/wiki/Exotic_animal "Exotic animal"). Prior to its closing in 2019, it had roughly 700 animals[[44]](#cite_note-44) including [Siberian tigers](/wiki/Siberian_tiger "Siberian tiger"), lions, [polar wolves](/wiki/Polar_wolf "Polar wolf"), and monkeys. Frösö Zoo also had a tropical house, a biological museum and an [amusement park](/wiki/Amusement_park "Amusement park"). Outside of Östersund in the village of [Orrviken](/wiki/Orrviken "Orrviken") there is a moose zoo called [Moose Garden](/w/index.php?title=Moose_Garden&action=edit&redlink=1 "Moose Garden (page does not exist)"), allowing close encounters with tame moose.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/F%C3%A4rgfabriken_norr%2C_%C3%96stersund.jpg/250px-F%C3%A4rgfabriken_norr%2C_%C3%96stersund.jpg)](/wiki/File:F%C3%A4rgfabriken_norr,_%C3%96stersund.jpg)

Färgfabriken Norr

Färgfabriken ('the paint factory') is a centre for experimental culture based in Stockholm that portrays itself as a laboratory of contemporary art. A branch named *Färgfabriken Norr* was established in Östersund between April 2008 and January 2011.[[45]](#cite_note-45)

[Gaaltije](/w/index.php?title=Gaaltije&action=edit&redlink=1 "Gaaltije (page does not exist)"), the centre for [South Sami](/wiki/South_Sami "South Sami") culture, opened in 1999 and is a living source of knowledge for South Sami culture, history and business.

[Gamla Tingshuset](/w/index.php?title=Gamla_Tingshuset&action=edit&redlink=1 "Gamla Tingshuset (page does not exist)") holds a small cinema, a café, a small venue and practice halls. It is usually a meeting place for the town's youth.

Media
-----

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Media")]

The largest daily newspaper in Östersund is *[Östersunds-Posten](/wiki/%C3%96stersunds-Posten "Östersunds-Posten")* (ÖP) with a circulation of 30,000 copies[[47]](#cite_note-press-47) and the second largest is *[Länstidningen Östersund](/w/index.php?title=L%C3%A4nstidningen_%C3%96stersund&action=edit&redlink=1 "Länstidningen Östersund (page does not exist)")* (LT) with a circulation of 15,000 copies[[47]](#cite_note-press-47) (2006 for both). Like most Swedish newspaper they each have a political [editorial page](/wiki/Editorial_page "Editorial page"), views of the [Centre Party](/wiki/Centre_Party_(Sweden) "Centre Party (Sweden)") are expressed in ÖP and views of the [Swedish Social Democratic Party](/wiki/Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party "Swedish Social Democratic Party") are expressed in LT. *Länstidningen* is unique in Sweden, as it is the only Swedish newspaper with [press support](/wiki/Press_support "Press support") that has ever made itself non-dependent on state subsidy. [*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Much of the paper's success is ascribed to the then editor-in-chief awarded with the [Grand Journalism Award](/wiki/Stora_Journalistpriset "Stora Journalistpriset") (*Stora Journalistpriset*).[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Since 2006 the newspaper has been dependent on state subsidy. The media group [Mittmedia](/w/index.php?title=Mittmedia&action=edit&redlink=1 "Mittmedia (page does not exist)") has owned both newspapers since 2005.[[48]](#cite_note-48)

Two [free daily newspapers](/wiki/Free_daily_newspaper "Free daily newspaper") exist in the city, *[100 procent Östersund](/w/index.php?title=100_procent_%C3%96stersund&action=edit&redlink=1 "100 procent Östersund (page does not exist)")* and *[Lokaltidningen Storsjön](/w/index.php?title=Lokaltidningen_Storsj%C3%B6n&action=edit&redlink=1 "Lokaltidningen Storsjön (page does not exist)")*.

Local radio stations include [Radio Jämtland](/w/index.php?title=Radio_J%C3%A4mtland&action=edit&redlink=1 "Radio Jämtland (page does not exist)") (a part of [Sveriges Radio](/wiki/Sveriges_Radio "Sveriges Radio")), [One FM](/w/index.php?title=One_FM_(Sweden)&action=edit&redlink=1 "One FM (Sweden) (page does not exist)") and [Modern Times Group](/wiki/Modern_Times_Group "Modern Times Group")'s [Rix FM](/w/index.php?title=Rix_FM&action=edit&redlink=1 "Rix FM (page does not exist)").

Education
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Education")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Mittuniversitetet_%C3%96stersund.jpg/250px-Mittuniversitetet_%C3%96stersund.jpg)](/wiki/File:Mittuniversitetet_%C3%96stersund.jpg)

Mid Sweden university in Östersund

Östersund recently[*[when?](/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")*] became a university city and the [Mid Sweden University](/wiki/Mid_Sweden_University "Mid Sweden University") has its largest campus site in Östersund with well over 7,000 students. The Mid Sweden University was a [university college](/wiki/University_college#Sweden_and_Norway "University college") (*[högskola](/wiki/H%C3%B6gskola "Högskola")*) named *Mitthögskolan* until it was granted university status in 2005, making it the youngest university in Sweden. Mitthögskolan was the result of the merger between the University College of Sundsvall/[Härnösand](/wiki/H%C3%A4rn%C3%B6sand "Härnösand") (*Högskolan i Sundsvall/Härnösand*) and the University College of Östersund (*Högskolan i Östersund*)[[49]](#cite_note-49)

Östersund is a centre for the research in social sciences ([business administration](/wiki/Business_Administration "Business Administration"), [psychology](/wiki/Psychology "Psychology"), sociology and [political science](/wiki/Political_Science "Political Science")) and social work, whilst the research in Health Sciences is split between Östersund and Sundsvall.

The city has several secondary schools (*[gymnasieskolor](/wiki/Gymnasium_(school) "Gymnasium (school)")*) of which [Palmcrantzskolan](/w/index.php?title=Palmcrantzskolan&action=edit&redlink=1 "Palmcrantzskolan (page does not exist)") (PC) and [Wargentinsskolan](/w/index.php?title=Wargentinsskolan&action=edit&redlink=1 "Wargentinsskolan (page does not exist)") (Wargen) are the two largest. Among the smaller are Storsjögymnasiet, Östersund's gymnasieskola and Dille Gård Naturbruksgymnasium.

Sports
------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Sports")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/%C3%96stersunds_skidstadion_Biathlon_WC_2008.JPG/250px-%C3%96stersunds_skidstadion_Biathlon_WC_2008.JPG)](/wiki/File:%C3%96stersunds_skidstadion_Biathlon_WC_2008.JPG)

The ski stadium of Östersund

Östersund is marketed as the *Winter City* and has a long history of winter sports. It is internationally perhaps most known as one of the regular [Biathlon World Cup](/wiki/Biathlon_World_Cup "Biathlon World Cup") hosts in late-November and early-December. World Cup competitions have been held there since 1989.[[50]](#cite_note-50) The [Biathlon World Championship 1970](/wiki/Biathlon_World_Championship_1970 "Biathlon World Championship 1970") were hosted in Östersund in [1970](/wiki/Biathlon_World_Championship_1970 "Biathlon World Championship 1970"), [2008](/wiki/Biathlon_World_Championships_2008 "Biathlon World Championships 2008") and [2019](/wiki/Biathlon_World_Championships_2019 "Biathlon World Championships 2019").

The cross-country skiing stadium is located two kilometres (1.2 miles) from the city centre and is one of the most well-equipped and spectator friendly ski stadiums in Sweden. The stadium is also internationally renowned due to the topography of its ski tracks, the compact track-system and the fact that Östersund is usually quite a reliable locality for snow during the winter months. A number of [biathlon](/wiki/Biathlon "Biathlon") world cup races have been held at the stadium as well as several national championships in cross-country skiing.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/Vy_%C3%B6ver_%C3%96stersund_fr%C3%A5n_Gustavsbergsbacken_p%C3%A5_Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n.jpg/250px-Vy_%C3%B6ver_%C3%96stersund_fr%C3%A5n_Gustavsbergsbacken_p%C3%A5_Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n.jpg)](/wiki/File:Vy_%C3%B6ver_%C3%96stersund_fr%C3%A5n_Gustavsbergsbacken_p%C3%A5_Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n.jpg)

Östersund seen from the piste Gustavsbergsbacken

*Nationellt Vintersportcentrum* (NVC, Swedish Winter Sports Research Centre) is a research and training project run by the sports movement, the university, the municipality and the county council. The [Swedish Olympic Committee](/wiki/Swedish_Olympic_Committee "Swedish Olympic Committee") (SOC) use its lab for various tests.

Östersund, in association with the neighboring municipality of [Åre](/wiki/%C3%85re "Åre"), had plans to be the candidate of Sweden for the organization of the [XXII Olympic Winter Games](/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics "2014 Winter Olympics"), the [2014 Winter Olympics](/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics "2014 Winter Olympics"), but the candidacy proposal was rejected by the government. It would have been the fourth attempt of this city (after [1994](/wiki/1994_Winter_Olympics "1994 Winter Olympics") where Östersund lost [the bid](/wiki/Bids_for_Olympic_Games "Bids for Olympic Games") with the score 45–39 to [Lillehammer](/wiki/Lillehammer "Lillehammer") in the final round, [1998](/wiki/1998_Winter_Olympics "1998 Winter Olympics") and [2002](/wiki/2002_Winter_Olympics "2002 Winter Olympics")).

Östersund has a basketball team in Sweden's highest division ([Ligan](/wiki/Ligan_(basketball) "Ligan (basketball)")), [Jämtland Basket](/wiki/J%C3%A4mtland_Basket "Jämtland Basket").

Östersund's Fallskärmsklubb is the oldest of Sweden's drop zones and was formed in 1958. The very first civilian parachute jump was done actually on the ice of Storsjön in February 1956. The jumpers were officers from the Swedish Parachute rangers regiment that also wanted to jump on their spare time. Östersund's Fallskärmsklubb is today localized to Optand's airfields, approximately 13 km (8 mi) south from Östersund where the education of students and skydiving for experienced jumpers are carried out year-round with the exception of late autumn until early winter.

Other sports clubs include:

* [IFK Östersund](/wiki/IFK_%C3%96stersund "IFK Östersund")
* [Ope IF](/wiki/Ope_IF "Ope IF")
* [Östersunds FK](/wiki/%C3%96stersunds_FK "Östersunds FK")
* [Fältjägarnas IF](/wiki/F%C3%A4ltj%C3%A4garnas_IF "Fältjägarnas IF")

### 2021 Special Olympics World Winter Games

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%96stersund&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: 2021 Special Olympics World Winter Games")]

Östersund along with [Åre](/wiki/%C3%85re "Åre") were originally to host the [2021 Special Olympics World Winter Games](/wiki/2021_Special_Olympics_World_Winter_Games "2021 Special Olympics World Winter Games"). It would have marked the first time that Sweden had ever hosted the Special Olympics.[[51]](#cite_note-51) However, due to lack of funding on 19 December 2019, the event did not take place in Sweden.[[52]](#cite_note-52) Instead it was to take place in [Kazan](/wiki/Kazan "Kazan"), Russia and was delayed to 2022 but was cancelled following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This article is about monarchs ruling over Germany after the 843 Treaty of Verdun. For ancient German/Germanic kings before the treaty, see [List of Frankish kings](/wiki/List_of_Frankish_kings "List of Frankish kings"). For German monarchs who lost their thrones in 1918, see [List of German monarchs in 1918](/wiki/List_of_German_monarchs_in_1918 "List of German monarchs in 1918").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/HRR_10Jh.jpg/250px-HRR_10Jh.jpg)](/wiki/File:HRR_10Jh.jpg)

German kingdom (blue) in the Holy Roman Empire around 1000

This is a list of monarchs who ruled over [East Francia](/wiki/East_Francia "East Francia"), and the [Kingdom of Germany](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Germany "Kingdom of Germany") ([Latin](/wiki/Latin_language "Latin language"): *Regnum Teutonicum*), from [the division](/wiki/Treaty_of_Verdun "Treaty of Verdun") of the [Frankish Empire](/wiki/Francia "Francia") in 843 and [the collapse](/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Holy_Roman_Empire "Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire") of the [Holy Roman Empire](/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire "Holy Roman Empire") in 1806 until [the collapse](/wiki/German_Revolution_of_1918%E2%80%931919 "German Revolution of 1918–1919") of the [German Empire](/wiki/German_Empire "German Empire") in 1918:

Holy Roman Empire (962–1806)
----------------------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=List_of_monarchs_of_Germany&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Holy Roman Empire (962–1806)")]

The title "[King of the Romans](/wiki/King_of_the_Romans "King of the Romans")", used in the [Holy Roman Empire](/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire "Holy Roman Empire"), denoted a ruler elected by the German princes whose authority was primarily exercised over the Germanic-speaking territories of the empire. While no formal “King of Germany” existed, the king’s election and governance effectively corresponded to that of a monarch over these lands. After election, the king would traditionally proceed to Rome to be [crowned emperor by the pope](/wiki/Coronation_of_the_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Coronation of the Holy Roman Emperor").
